transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Lena Cho (Redwood) — Jared Morales, Priya Raman, Sara Liang (Aurelia)

Summary: quick triage of recent pilot runs; focused on why first-token variance spiked on Tuesday, discuss kernel routing idea ("kernel-shaped routes"), and plan microburst profiling with KV cache toggles. Action: bench runs and kernel selection matrix to decide canary rollout policy.

Topics: TTFT variance, streaming handshake delays, sequence-length distribution, kernel choice tradeoffs, hedging/priority queueing, security/production readiness notes (KMS/SOC2 questions).

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: alright everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep to 45ish minutes but we have 54 on the calendar so more than enough. quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Jared: Jared here, platform.
[00:00:12] Priya: Priya — ml infra.
[00:00:14] Sara: Sara — product.
[00:00:16] Lena: Lena, se on the redwood side.
[00:00:18] Samir: great. so recap — last week we saw a ttft spike in the evening window, microburst-y. Lena you ran some kernel traces?
[00:00:28] Lena: yea i ran the trace deck — sorry some of the labels got munged in the export so you'll see e.g. KV cache appearing as "K V" in the trace. but the core is that the early-token path switched kernels at ~16ms for a subset of requests, which added jitter.
[00:00:45] Priya: wait "switched kernels" meaning different gemm kernels or different attention implementation?
[00:00:51] Lena: different attention microkernels — the selection heuristic chose a striping kernel when seq len was misclassified as long, so for short sequences it burned extra cycles. policy threshold tuned at runtime misfired under that sample distribution.
[00:01:08] Sara: so could that be the seq len histogram we saw from staging vs prod — prod has a fat tail?
[00:01:14] Jared: exactly, our prod 95th percentile is like 420 tokens because of a few agents doing long transcripts, but our median is 18.
[00:01:22] Samir: classic mixed workload. that's why we're exploring kernel-shaped routes — route requests to kernels based on a lightweight fast-path classifier instead of raw seqlen heuristic.
[00:01:34] Priya: can you explain "kernel-shaped routes" in plain english?
[00:01:36] Lena: sure — think of it like network routing but for kernel selection: a tiny classifier (few features: initial prompt length, user role tag, presence of streaming flag) decides which kernel bucket to land in — optimized for first-token latency or amortized throughput.
[00:01:54] Sara: i like it but i'm worried about extra inference overhead from the classifier itself adding to ttft.
[00:01:59] Lena: good point — classifier is a cheap table lookup + a 1-2 token model if needed; cost is microsecond-tier, we estimated <1ms. for many of your median requests it's still net win because we avoid the wrong kernel path.
[00:02:12] Jared: our main SLO is p50 < 35ms ttft and p99 < 110ms — those microbursts push p99 past target.
[00:02:20] Samir: right — so two levers: better routing + KV cache priming. we saw in the Tuesday run that KV priming reduced median by ~6ms but didn't help for the misrouted kernel cases.
[00:02:33] Priya: when you say KV priming was enabled was that prefix-KV or global warm cache?
[00:02:37] Lena: prefix only — we prefilled with common system prompts. global warm was off for resource reasons.
[00:02:41] Sara: can we enable global warm for the pilot? what's the cost?
[00:02:44] Samir: cost delta is small for small pools but grows with dedicated capacity. i'll include pricing numbers in the follow-up — tradeoff there.
[00:02:51] [00:03:00] Jared: are there any security blockers if we enable more aggressive caching? aurelia is under HIPAA-ish constraints.
[00:03:06] Priya: yeah we need encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs — we also need SSO/SAML working for the console.
[00:03:12] Lena: Redwood private supports customer KMS and audit logging; for the hosted pilot we use envelope encryption but we can show the SOC 2 artifact.
[00:03:21] Samir: noted — i'll add SOC2 and KMS docs to the repo link after the call.
[00:03:25] [00:03:40] Lena: back to latency — i pushed a small kernel-sel change that biases towards stream-optimized kernels when we detect streaming=true in the header. in the canary it dropped first token for stream clients by ~9ms.
[00:03:52] Sara: the streaming clients are our highest volume; that's promising. what about edge cases where a streamed request is actually long? we don't want to waste throughput.
[00:04:00] Lena: we hedge — if tokens stream in past a threshold we splice in the heavier kernel on the next batch, so worst-case we pay a small transition cost.
[00:04:07] Priya: and hedging means duplicate the first token to two kernels? that could double work.
[00:04:12] Lena: good catch — we don't duplicate full work. we run a tiny fastpath for token 1 then switch; duplication only for a 1-2 token window if needed. it's a micro-hedge not full duplication.
[00:04:22] Jared: can you share numbers from the canary? mean/median/99?
[00:04:26] Lena: sure — quick stats from canary (10k requests): ttft p50 28ms (vs 34 baseline), p90 62ms (vs 68), p99 128ms (vs 140) — but the subset misrouted had p99 spikes to 210, so need to fix the routing model.
[00:04:47] Samir: so action a: refine routing classifier with a small loss function tuned to minimize the p99 for ttft. action b: run microburst bench with and without KV cache and compare.
[00:04:58] Sara: do you have the bench harness? we want to replicate locally as well.
[00:05:02] Lena: yes i'll check in the harness scripts and a quick README. note the harness depends on the kernel debug traces which sometimes change names across runtime builds — small pain.
[00:05:12] [00:05:30] Priya: unrelated but important: does private deployment change kernel choices? if we run in our vpc with dedicated gpus can we force certain kernels?
[00:05:38] Lena: in dedicated mode you can pin certain runtime knobs and preselect kernel profiles more aggressively — less risk of misclassification because you control the sw stack. but there are tradeoffs around throughput efficiency and cost.
[00:05:49] Samir: and dedicated gives you reserved burst too which helps microbursts but costs more.
[00:05:55] Jared: can we get a matrix showing dedicated vs hosted latency/cost curves for our workload?
[00:06:01] Samir: yes — i'll produce a simple delta matrix + cost per 1M tokens with reserved-burst options.
[00:06:07] Sara: any competitor notes? we evaluated GoliathAI but they didn't expose kernel control; CloudEndpoints had better pricing but worse streaming paths.
[00:06:16] Lena: that's been our read too.
[00:06:20] [00:06:35] Jared: ok next area — sequence-length distribution. we agreed to upload the histogram. i flagged that our staging sample underrepresents long tails.
[00:06:43] Priya: yes, i will attach the prod histogram to the drive after this call. it's the same artifact I mentioned in the pilot doc.
[00:06:50] Samir: perfect — that will feed the classifier training set.
[00:06:54] Lena: also i'm going to try a hybrid policy: if median < X then route to lightweight kernel else use baseline. we need the correct X from their histogram.
[00:07:05] Sara: can we set X dynamically based on short-term traffic patterns?
[00:07:08] Lena: yes, we can do a sliding-window threshold, though it introduces another parameter. we'd prefer to start static then iterate.
[00:07:16] [00:07:40] Jared: question about observability — when the misroute happens our dashboard currently shows only end-to-end latency and kernel label as a free-text field. can we add an alert on kernel-switch frequency?
[00:07:52] Lena: yes we can emit metric kernel_selector.flip_rate and wire up an alert for > 0.5% flips in a 5m window.
[00:07:58] Samir: we'll add that to the dashboard update Samir will share.
[00:08:05] [00:08:20] Priya: we also need to be careful about A/Bing kernels for compliance — audit must show consistent behavior for certain user classes.
[00:08:28] Samir: noted, we'll ensure rollout policies tag experiments and persist selection decisions in the audit log so you can review.
[00:08:35] [00:08:50] Sara: what about quantization — have you tried 4-bit on the short-kernel path?
[00:08:55] Lena: yes short-kernel supports q4 with minimal quality loss for short completion tasks; it shaves another ~3-6ms. we can propose a quantized kernel for the fast path.
[00:09:06] Priya: any quality regressions we should be worried about for our clinical prompts?
[00:09:10] Lena: we ran a small eval set; most metrics stable but one prompt family had hallucination drift at q4. we'll include that in the results so you can decide which prompts to whitelist for non-quantized mode.
[00:09:20] [00:09:40] Jared: ok, i'd like to schedule two runs: 1) the 1k microburst bench with KV toggles, 2) a 10k canary with kernel-shaped routing + quantized fast-path. how long to complete?
[00:09:52] Lena: microburst bench ~2 days to run proper sampling and analysis; canary 3-4 days incl. rollout and data collection.
[00:09:58] Samir: timeline fits our calendar — that would put us in good shape for a pilot decision mid-next-week.
[00:10:05] [00:10:20] Sara: one last piece — pricing for dedicated reserved burst vs hosted with autoscale.
[00:10:25] Samir: i'll include delta and show examples for your current QPS and expected peak microburst.
[00:10:30] [00:10:45] Priya: on security — can you confirm the hosted pilot keeps PII out of logs by default?
[00:10:52] Lena: yes we have an option to redact PII at ingest and disable retention; for additional assurance we can send our data flow diagram.
[00:10:59] Jared: great.
[00:11:10] [00:11:40] Samir: ok let's recap and assign owners.
[00:11:45] Recap:
- Action: Lena to run microburst bench (KV on/off) and post results (owner: Lena, due 2026-03-30).
- Action: Jared to upload prod seqlen histogram (owner: Jared, due 2026-03-31).
- Action: Samir to send kernel selection matrix, pricing delta, SOC2+KMS docs (owner: Samir, due 2026-04-01).

[00:12:10] Lena: i'll also attach the harness and note any differences in trace labels.
[00:12:15] Sara: thanks — i want to see the p99 delta before committing to dedicated.
[00:12:20] Samir: understood. we'll prioritize p99 ttft and a small canary on streaming clients.
[00:12:26] [00:12:40] Priya: any blockers from our side? i just need to get permissions to the shared drive for the harness.
[00:12:45] Samir: i'll send the link and request access; Samir will also create a ticket in your tracker with the bench steps.
[00:12:52] Jared: one more nit — can the dashboard show kernel label the moment of first token not end to end? helps debug.
[00:12:58] Lena: yes we'll emit first-token kernel label metric.
[00:13:10] [00:13:30] Samir: ok perfect. anything else?
[00:13:32] Sara: nope, thanks everyone.
[00:13:34] Samir: thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and set next sync for 03-31 or earlier depending on results.

[00:13:45] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels in export (Speaker 3 sometimes merged with Speaker 1), some technical terms spelled out with spaces (e.g., "K V"), minor filler words and crosstalk preserved.
